title: Moderna reports first positive Phase 3 results for mRNA neoantigen therapy in melanoma
summary: Moderna and Merck announced positive Phase 3 trial results for 'intismeran autogene,' an individualized mRNA-based neoantigen therapy for melanoma, used in combination with KEYTRUDA. The trial met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival and a key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival. This marks the first successful Phase 3 result for an individualized neoantigen therapy and an mRNA-based cancer treatment, representing a significant milestone in mRNA medicine development.
key_points: Moderna and Merck reported positive Phase 3 results for 'intismeran autogene,' an mRNA-based individualized neoantigen therapy for melanoma.
The therapy was tested in combination with KEYTRUDA in patients with completely resected stage IIB-IV melanoma.
The trial met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival and a key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival.
This is the first successful Phase 3 result for an individualized neoantigen therapy and an mRNA-based cancer treatment.
The milestone highlights the potential of mRNA technology beyond vaccines, particularly in personalized cancer treatment.
The achievement reflects over a decade of research and perseverance in mRNA medicine development.
